status.en: 45 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Sinaloa, Mexico City and Morelos.
status.nb: 45 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Sinaloa, Mexico City og Morelos.

summary.en: Violence in Mexico remains acute, with 46 armed incidents reported in the last week, concentrated in Sinaloa, Mexico City and Ensenada, and four of those reported by multiple sources. Prison unrest continues, as fresh clashes in Sinaloa prisons left two dead and a separate riot in Mazatlán claimed 12 lives. Journalists are being targeted, highlighted by the killing of Hamurabi Huesca Manzano in Oaxaca and another journalist killed earlier this year. The UCDP recorded 37 battle‑related deaths in 1996, underscoring the long‑standing lethal nature of the conflict.
summary.nb: Vold i Mexico er fortsatt intens, med 46 væpnede hendelser rapportert siste uke, konsentrert i Sinaloa, Mexico City og Ensenada, og fire av dem ble dekket av flere kilder. Fengselsuroen pågår, med nye sammenstøt i Sinaloa-fengsler som drepte to og en separat opptøye i Mazatlán som krevde 12 liv. Journalister blir målrettet, tydeliggjort av drapet på Hamurabi Huesca Manzano i Oaxaca og en annen journalist drept tidligere i år. UCDP registrerte 37 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 1996, som understreker den langvarige dødelige karakteren av konflikten.

background.title: Mexican drug war
background.extract: The Mexican drug war is an ongoing asymmetric armed conflict between the Mexican government and various drug trafficking syndicates. When the Mexican military intervened in 2006, the government's main objective was to reduce drug-related violence. The Mexican government has asserted that its primary focus is on dismantling the cartels and preventing drug trafficking. The conflict has been described as the Mexican theater of the global war on drugs, as led by the United States federal government. Analysts estimate wholesale earnings from illicit drug sales range from $13.6 to $49.4 billion annually.
